title: The Immortal Game
intro: Anderssen gives up a bishop, both rooks and his queen, and mates with three minor pieces.

title: The Evergreen Game
intro: An Evans Gambit that ends with a quiet rook move and a queen sacrifice leading to mate.

title: Morphy's queen sacrifice
intro: Morphy sacrifices his queen for a bishop to tear open the white king's shelter.

title: The Opera Game
intro: The model lesson in rapid development: every white move brings a piece into the attack.

title: Zukertort's Immortal
intro: A queen offered on b4 that cannot be taken, followed by a rook sacrifice on the eighth rank.

title: The double bishop sacrifice
intro: Lasker sacrifices both bishops on h7 and g7 to strip the black king bare.

title: Steinitz's rook on the seventh
intro: A rook that cannot be captured walks along the seventh rank while all of White's pieces hang.

title: Rubinstein's Immortal
intro: Black's pieces flood the kingside; queen and rook are both offered in a single combination.

title: The Gold Coins Game
intro: Marshall's final queen move, placing it where three pieces can take it, is one of the most famous ever played.

title: Lasker's Exchange Variation
intro: Needing a win, Lasker chooses a quiet opening and squeezes Capablanca with a space advantage.

title: The Marshall Attack is born
intro: Marshall springs his prepared gambit; Capablanca defends coolly over the board and wins.

title: Alekhine's three queens
intro: Black plays on the whole board and promotes pawn after pawn in a game Alekhine counted among his best.

title: The Immortal Zugzwang Game
intro: With the board still full of pieces, White runs out of moves that do not lose material.

title: Capablanca's rook ending
intro: A textbook rook endgame: White gives up pawns to get his king and rook into the attack.

title: Alekhine's long combination
intro: A rook lands on e3 where it cannot be taken, starting a combination more than ten moves deep.

title: The Windmill
intro: A queen sacrifice sets up a rook and bishop that check and capture, over and over.

title: The Polish Immortal
intro: Najdorf sacrifices all four minor pieces to drag the white king up the board to its mate.

title: Botvinnik's bishop sacrifice
intro: A bishop goes to a3 and then a knight is given too, all to escort one passed pawn.

title: The Game of the Century
intro: Thirteen-year-old Fischer gives up his queen and wins with a swarm of minor pieces.

title: Tal's knight on f4
intro: Tal leaves a knight to be taken for the sake of open lines, and the complications prove too much.

title: Fischer–Spassky, game 6
intro: Fischer opens with the c-pawn for once and wins so smoothly that Spassky joined the applause.

title: Kasparov's Immortal
intro: A rook sacrifice on d4 begins a king hunt that chases Black's king from one side of the board to the other.
